manifest.board: ClockworkPi PicoCalc + Raspberry Pi Pico H

arena_validation.scope: All linked normal text/rodata inputs from the five owned math objects retain V75 input sizes/order and low 13 address bits. External SDK wrapper placement and other-core/IRQ cache traffic are not fixed by this check.

result.scope: Every allocated code/data payload of all five owned math objects is byte-identical before linking. Only link placement and relocation targets change; no new numerical instructions or coefficient data.

current.ABI: R0 binary32 input, R0/R1 binary64 output; R4-R11 and SP preserved

result.oracle: Integer IEEE binary32 significand widening; every finite binary32 value is exactly representable as binary64. NaN sign/payload are preserved and signaling NaNs quieted.
result.scope: Both signs, all 256 exponent encodings, significand bit boundaries and deterministic random encodings. This finite ARM test is not exhaustive over all 2^32 inputs, and instruction/read counts are not physical timings.

baseline.ABI: R0 binary32 input, R0/R1 binary64 output; R4-R11 and SP preserved

result.scope: Cortex-M4 O3 release, both soft and hard float ABIs: normalized preprocessing and every allocated code/data section identical; existing M4 runtime sources byte-identical
Non-RP2040 generic ARMv6-M: every allocated code/data section remains byte-identical to V60. The generic spelling has an extra expression macro; normalized preprocessing identity is not claimed.

Direct exact-stage ARM calls including all saved registers, SP, stack writes, signed exponents, subnormal/overflow output and a pending SIO divider. Finite implementation qualification; domain argument is separate.
The production layout passes unchanged; changing one instruction byte inside an internal exact-pow helper is rejected. No firmware execution or hardware access.

result.scope: Static production BL/BLX calls to the owned EABI double helpers in fixed cold text; no wrapped alternatives for these four names. Does not enumerate indirect native-API calls or prove instruction timing.

result.scope: Real ARM math and timing APP source. Timer/storage/UI/XIP counters mocked; this is a protocol and ABI test, not a cycle benchmark.

rounding.oracle: Directed MPFR bounds; both endpoints round to the same binary64 (RNE).
rounding.abi: Every call verifies R4-R11, SP, bounded stack writes.
rounding.semantics: RNE return values; errno and floating exception flags are not implemented.
rounding.nan_result_policy: NaN results must be quiet; payload and sign are unspecified.
known_limitations: An undecided owned 1024-bit pow refinement still traps; all-input totality is unproved.
rounding.scope: Finite corpus, not an exhaustive proof over every binary64 input.

ports/picocalc/CMakeLists.txt.scope: Arena insertion only; preserve other current ROOT CMake changes

cache_model.assumptions: LRU and FIFO replacement and whole-line and per-word fill are modeled separately; these four models are assumptions, not claims about undocumented replacement or prefetch behavior.
cache_model.scope: Exact owned ARM instruction/data traces and results for the three gaps; isolated owned function calls only. Excludes the other core, IRQ traffic, caller prefetch and Qfplib batches. The third corpus pass is modeled after two warm passes. Model miss counts are not measured XIP counters or timings.

remains: Wait for platform acceptance and the agreed memory-function window, then obtain explicit device release and the final immutable source/restore. The current 7AEA snapshot is unaccepted.
Rebase the arena onto that final platform, verify owned object payloads/addresses and resources, and qualify before hardware timing.
Measure the complete 114-group hardware matrix, including the three V72 speed gaps. Isolated cache models and instruction counts do not establish speed parity.
General binary64 pow totality outside the 224 exact-stage exponent values remains unproved; the final undecided trap is retained.
